conventions.convention: Assume AC and a finite horizon T≥0. States start at X₀; observations start at Y₁. The empty observation history is a singleton and its filter is μ₀.

State and observation spaces are standard Borel. Filtering, prediction and full-path smoothing are data-indexed probability kernels satisfying conditional event identities; their values on measurable observation-null sets need not be unique.

Each observation density is supplied jointly product-measurable against a sigma-finite reference measure and integrates to one for every state. Normalize only at finite positive evidence; at zero or infinite evidence use the predictive probability as filler.

The scalar Gaussian example uses Borel scalar spaces and Lebesgue measure restricted to the Borel sigma-algebra. Its value at Y₁=2 is the version selected by the supplied density formula, not a uniquely determined conditional value.

load_bearing.statement: Filtering and predictive kernels are probability kernels whose compositions with the respective observation histories are RCDs of the current state; a finite-horizon smoothing kernel similarly conditions the full state path on all observations.

Assume AC and the finite-horizon standard-Borel kernel model. With specified product-measurable normalized observation densities against sigma-finite measures, propagation of a previous filtering kernel is predictive, and its finite-positive-evidence Bayes update with predictive filler is filtering. For each fixed history, both zero and infinite evidence fibers have zero mass under the observation marginal determined by that predictive version.

Under AC, a finite-horizon state-space model with standard-Borel state and observation spaces, an initial probability and transition and observation probability kernels has data-indexed filtering and predictive kernels and a full-path smoothing kernel, including T=0.

Initialize π₀=μ₀; at each time propagate through Kₜ, integrate the observation density to obtain evidence, and normalize on finite positive evidence, otherwise returning the predictive measure. Return π₀ and all time-indexed predictions, evidence functions and filters.

seams_checked.note: Both sides require finite positive evidence for normalization. The filtering algorithm supplies a proper predictive probability, jointly measurable normalized observation densities and sigma-finite reference measures, matching the published dominated Bayes theorem. It makes no improper-prior predictive claim.

The Kalman algorithm and exactness theorem use the filtering-kernel definition and standard-Borel existence result with AC and the singleton initial history. Their exactness statement preserves conditional-version freedom on null histories and does not infer observation-density assumptions from general existence.

The Feynman–Kac target definition cites filtering laws only for their conditional-version interpretation and explicitly disclaims selection of pointwise conditional values on observation-null histories. Its normalized path targets require finite positive normalizers.
